utterances.text: I would rather break now with your leave, Your Honour, because we have to find one document that would clarify whether there was VRS in Foca area or not because it was -- I don't have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fine. If you say the questions put by Mr. Traldi require that I would have another --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably five minutes. I need not more than five, six minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But you prefer to have that after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's understood. We'll take the break and we will resume at quarter past midday, and we'd like to see the witness back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first establish whether the videolink is still functioning well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, I can confirm we can see and we can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't see you, I don't hear you. And I hope I pushed the right button.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we can see you and we can hear you. Can you see and hear us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I now can see you and I can hear you. So apparently it's functioning well. Mr. Lukic will now put some questions in re-examination to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krnojelac, good afternoon, once again.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR KRNOJELAC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether you'll manage to see this, but I'm going to read something out to you and I'm going to call it up for the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P2838.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For you, Mr. Krnojelac, I'd like to explain what this is about. This is a document of the Foca tactical group of the Serb republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina dated the 29th of June, 1992, that is to say, seven days after you were wounded this document was written up. Let us now just look at the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that would be page 2 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see that the document was signed by the commander, Colonel Marko Kovac. And from the stamp, we can see what Colonel Kovac was commander of at the time. It was the staff of the Territorial Defence of the Serb Municipality of Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So let us go back to the first page now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's a minor matter but I'm not sure if Mr. Lukic is suggesting there's an error in the translation. The stamp is a little bit small but it refers -- the translation, anyway, refers to the SAO Herzegovina rather than to the municipality of Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Inner circle. If we can have the stamp on our screens enlarged. More, more, more, more -- yeah. On the bottom part of this -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you read it in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you read what exactly, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'll read top part outer circle. [Interpretation] "Serb republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." [In English] In the middle --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the bottom part reads what?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Serb municipality of Foca."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And now you read the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Middle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- middle circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Serb autonomous district of Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now you read the inner circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Territorial Defence staff."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think we've read now the whole of the stamp and we were able to follow it in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So in the English, I can see now it's missing, so that's probably why my learned friend was objecting. It's missing Serbian municipality of Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And having been pointed to that, we agree that line is missing and also that the line that is present in the translation about the autonomous district is also present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then having clarified this, Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Krnojelac, you were asked whether at that time -- actually, you said that the Army of Republika Srpska did not exist at that time, before you were wounded in the territory of the municipality of Foca. And we are saying that this is exactly confirmed by this document tendered by the Prosecution. We can go through the entire document and we can see that it is the future tense that is used when it is stated, "I hereby order using the mobilised and armed men establish the following ..." and then it says the Foca tactical group, the 1st Foca Infantry Brigade, the 2nd Foca Infantry Brigade. And then paragraph 4, a deadline is provided in terms of when this should start, so it says, paragraph 4, the units are to be established as of the 5th of July, 1992, and so on and so forth. So would you stand by what you said, that the Army of Republika Srpska had not been established?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR KRNOJELAC
utterances.text: Yes. And I claim with full responsibility that the army of Republika Srpska did not exist before I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Lukic, it's all fine. It's as leading as possibly could be. At the same time, it's not for the first time that we see that stamps are used which are not always updated, and you are leading because in the document itself, not in a stamp, which can have existed and put there, I think in the document itself, on the first page, it talks about the Vojska of Republika Srpska, and now to say, isn't it, that this all confirms is not only leading but is also improperly suggesting conclusions which should be kept for a later stage in the proceedings, because if I look at the document itself -- let me just have a look again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say this document clearly shows, pointing at the -- that the VRS did not exist yet at this point in time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we see the first page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the area of Foca. Not that it did not exist at all. In the area of Foca, it did not function.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Functioning or existing is not the same, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or existing in the area of Foca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But what I see is that -- and we are now talking about Foca tactical group.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Based on the order of the GS, the Main Staff --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of the army of the Serbian republic. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, if you go further -- no, no, no, no, no. If you go further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of BH.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot follow where Mr. Lukic is reading from. Could we please have a reference. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we are reading in the English from the first paragraph. Okay. But whatever the case is, Mr. Lukic, this is argument rather than examination of a witness. To put certain portions of a document to him and to ask him whether this confirms or not, you may argue that, there's no problem about that, but it's not a question you put to a witness. And it may well be debatable what is the right conclusion to be drawn in the context of the whole of the evidence rather than to put a stamp to a witness and ask him, doesn't this confirm the situation. Whether it does or not is not for the witness to decide. It's not a question of fact. You can ask him whether the stamp reads what it reads. You don't have to ask that to him because you can just read it and we'll follow you and Mr. Traldi fully agreed with you. There is a need to have it translated -- at least to provide a new translation, but I find this not a proper way of examining a witness in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, only one addition. Your question was not related to Foca. Your question was: "So would you stand by what you said, that the Army of Republika Srpska had not been established." Which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My mistake, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's leave this quickly behind us. If you have any further questions, Mr. Lukic, you may put them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, only it was suggested to the witness that he was not telling the truth that there was, and even in the last testimony at his father's trial and at this testimony he was very firm in his statement that there was no VRS in the Foca area. He was not testifying about other parts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you are arguing again. Reliability and credibility of the witness can be discussed before the court through the parties. If there's any question of fact which might shed further light on this matter, you may put it, but not to ask the witness to -- whether he agrees or not that a certain stamp would confirm what he said before. That's not a task for a witness. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krnojelac, we see Mr. Kovac mentioned here. Perhaps you do know, perhaps you don't know, what was his position before you were wounded, and was he in Foca at all?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR KRNOJELAC
utterances.text: I claim with full responsibility that this man was not in Foca while I was a soldier, so he came only after I was wounded. Which positions he held before that, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The question of whether battalions were established was discussed, page 28, line 4. The transcript from your testimony in your late father's trial was put to you. Did anyone inform you about which units were established? Did anyone report to you about that? Did you know at all which units could have been formed in Foca?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR KRNOJELAC
utterances.text: No, nobody gave information about that. And I still claim that as far as I know there weren't any battalions up until when I was wounded. Later on when the VRS was established, then brigades and battalions and whatever was established, but before I was wounded that certainly did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now take a look at 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I put some additional questions. In the trial of your father, you talked about battalions. Today, you say there were no battalions. And now you tell us that -- first of all you tell us that no one informed you about what was established and what was not established. And after that, you say the battalions were only established at a later stage. That is all -- at least has contradictory elements as inconsistent elements. If nobody gave you information about that, how would you still know that the brigades and the battalions were not established before you were wounded if no one informed about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know if I understood Mr. Lukic's question properly. Nobody informed me in that period while I was a soldier. Later on, in this period after my wounding, I know about that from my brother and from other comrades in the unit that the Army of Republika Srpska was established and that units were established then, battalions, brigades, whatever. But while I was a soldier, that certainly did not exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you have no personal knowledge about it but this is what you heard from your brother and from the other comrades at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know to what extent you heard me. I claim and guarantee that until the 22nd of June, 1992, that is the date when I was wounded, up until that moment there was no Army of Republika Srpska or any battalions that were in existence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under oath --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know about that because I was present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under -- after having given your solemn declaration in the trial of your father, you testified about battalions, and now you're telling us that you claim and guarantee that they were not there. That, at least, is not consistent. Do you have an explanation as why you gave a different testimony in your father's case against what you told us today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know who translated that and how they translated that, but I'm telling you I would like you to show me this recording where I'm saying that. And I assert that I certainly did not say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To inform the parties, CLSS is working at this moment on reviewing the audio. Perhaps not during the testimony of this witness the results will be available, but I hope that they are available very soon. I'll later instruct the witness not to communicate with anyone in the usual way so that the parties still would have an opportunity to see whether they wanted to further pursue the accuracy of that matter or leave it as it is with the knowledge of the outcome of the CLSS verification. The witness again, now, has stated that it must be a mistake and we have -- luckily enough we have an opportunity to verify that and that's what's done. Any further questions, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we may see the document 65 ter, from the Prosecution list, 14203.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krnojelac, I don't know whether you can see this in front of you, this document on the screen. Can you see it or not?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR KRNOJELAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to tell you what this is all about. It's a very short document. It says the Serb republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Serbian municipality of Foca, penal and correctional facility Foca, that KP Dom Foca. The date is the 15th of May, 1992. And this document is being sent to the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Foca. And it says in the text: "Please find enclosed the request of detainee Enes Zekovic for release from detention. We are forwarding to you for further action. We received the request on the 15th of May this year." Attachments one. And the signature says acting warden Milorad Krnojelac. At that time, you were still by your father. Did you know, did your father tell you that he could not release detainees and prisoners from the KP Dom Foca, or rather that this was done by the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Foca?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR KRNOJELAC
utterances.text: As the document itself shows, he absolutely had nothing to do with the detainees at the KP Dom Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we deal with that, could the witness tell us whether Enes Zekovic, whether he knows this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not know Mr. Enes Zekovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judging by the name, but perhaps I should address the parties, would you expect this to be a Muslim or a Serb or a Croat or whatever? Would you -- would the name -- if the parties would agree on that, we don't have to ask the witness because we are asking more or less for a judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We agree that's a Muslim person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a Muslim person. Parties agree on that. Okay. That's fine. Then we don't have to put the question to the witness. Any further questions -- no, first admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D651, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D651 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was mentioned to you that in the apartment that was allocated to you by the municipality on a temporary basis, Atif worked there and you said yes, that's a Muslim. This Atif, did he visit you after the war? Did you see him ever?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR KRNOJELAC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, although during my father's trial, I brought a letter that he had sent me during the war where he is thanking me for having helped him and having informed his family that he was alive and well. Two years ago he came to Foca, we had coffee, we talked, which means that the man is alive and well to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krnojelac. That is all we had for you. Thank you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I meanwhile can inform the parties, I asked already to be informally briefed on the outcome, and again therefore this is informal, but I received an e-mail which states the B/C/S of what the witness said and the English interpretation, as recorded in the transcript, that's what my e-mail reads, the provisional review of CLSS is the interpretation is correct, and I see both in the B/C/S and in the English text, and we of course will share that with the parties, the word -- at least the word "battalion" in -- which in B/C/S apparently is the same, more or less, as in English, and the reference to the 1st Battalion. If the parties feel any need to further pursue this matter, then of course they have an opportunity to do so, but I asked for an alarming signal if there would be something wrong and it appears from this first report that at least it was not, not any error or even let alone a major error was detected upon the first review. Let me first share it with my colleagues and then I'll share it with the parties. No further questions, Mr. Lukic? Any further questions, Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Very briefly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have P2838 back, the first document Mr. Lukic used on re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, looking at point one here on page 1 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And on page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, the witness can't see it. So you have to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It should be part of his packet.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, witness has the document in front of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's available to the witness. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's under point 1 in the B/C/S. And if we could turn to page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's talking about the formation of the tactical group and the brigades, and it says: "1st light brigade out of 2b, 3b, and 7b, 2nd light brigade out of 1b, 4b, 5b, and 6b." And I think it's fair, sir, to put to you that our case is that refers to the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, and 7th Battalions that existed already at this point. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR KRNOJELAC
utterances.text: Sir, as far as I can see, this is dated 29 June. I left on the 22nd June and I maintain that until the 22nd June, while I was still a combatant in the brigade, there was no battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No loud speaking, Mr. Mladic. One question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If this document says that a light infantry brigade, the Foca Light Infantry Brigade is to composed of men from certain battalions, and if you emphasise that this document dates from the 29th of June, that would mean that between, I think it was the 22nd when you were wounded, that in one week they would first have to establish the battalions, and then to establish the Foca Light Infantry Brigade to composed of men from these battalions which were created -- within the six or seven days before. If you would like to comment on that, you have an opportunity to do so, but you don't have to.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR KRNOJELAC
utterances.text: I'm really not a military expert to be able to know how this is established and how it's done, but I say with full responsibility that the Army of Republika Srpska did not exist until the 22nd June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. No further questions from the Bench. Witness, I'd like to thank you very much for making yourself available as a witness and coming to the videolink room, and I would also like to thank you for having answered the questions, questions that were put to you by the parties and questions that were put to you by the Bench. And I'm at this moment looking at the parties. There's no need to further instruct the witness. Then I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All my greetings to you. Best wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. The videolink can be ended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, what would you prefer? We can start with the next witness now. We had a bit of a delay this morning so there's another way of taking the break now so that you will have a bit more uninterrupted possibility to examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My colleague Stojanovic said that he's ready to continue immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Mr. Stojanovic you would also prefer to continue for 20 minutes, 25 minutes, and then have a break and then to -- or would you prefer to take a break first and then have some 55 minutes which is more, I think, than you asked for, with at least no risk of being interrupted halfway? Is it the latter that you prefer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour, and General Mladic suggested that we do it that way so I suggest we take a break now and then continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take the break first and we will resume -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the record, the parties will receive the provisional -- the first report which is not usual formal report as we receive it, but I think I've read that -- the major elements and you have not insisted on me instructing the witness in any other way, so therefore I take it that this, apart, perhaps, from the final report, that this determines this matter for the time being. We take a break and we resume at 20 minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will wait for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. Your next witness, Mr. Lukic, is Mr. Sokolovic -- or it's you, Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Sokolovic is your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll wait for him to enter the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Sokolovic, I presume. Mr. Sokolovic, may I invite you to make the solemn declaration, the text of which is now handed out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly swear that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sokolovic. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We just need to adjust this a little.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sokolovic, you will first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic, you find him to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Stojanovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Sokolovic. Would you kindly state your name and surname for the record.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Milorad Sokolovic. People call me Mile.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sokolovic, was there a time when you gave a written statement to the Defence team of General Mladic on the issues you were questioned about?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we call up in e-court 65 ter 1D01695.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sokolovic, this is the first time you are in this courtroom. You will see on the screen the first page of that statement. Could you tell the Court if the signature on this page is yours and if the personal details are correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are correct, and it's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On this page, is it again your signature and the date written in your hand?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Today, when you made the solemn declaration in the courtroom that you will speak the truth and nothing but the truth, would you answer in the same way as written in the statement and does it correspond to your best recollection?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The statement was made to the best of my recollection and if I were asked the same things today, I would answer the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that this is the right moment to tender the witness statement 1D01695 which is the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D652, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the absence of any objections, D652 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed if you have any further questions or if you want to read a summary, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, I will read a short summary of Milorad Sokolovic's witness statement, and I will emphasise that the beginning of the war found Milorad Sokolovic in his birthplace, Rogatica, where he was employed as the manager of the electricity distribution company and a deputy to the Municipal Assembly of Rogatica on behalf of the SDS. Before the war, he joins the Crisis Staff and accepts the duty of its president. He remained in this position until the end of May 1992, when the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Rogatica was formed, and he headed it until October 1993 when he returned to his company. The witness speaks about the agreements with the SDA Crisis Staff on the peaceful demarcation in the Rogatica municipality and the decision made by the assembly to divide the municipality into the Muslim and Serbian municipalities. He is familiar with the incidents of interethnic nature after the death of Serb civilians on St. George's day in 1992 and on 10 May 1992 in Zivaljevina village. The tensions culminated on 21st May, 1992, when a young man, Drazenko Mihaljevic was ambushed and killed and his dead body was not turned over to the family by the Muslims. So under the pressure of the local inhabitants, the commander of the then TO sent a message to the Muslims that if they do not wish to turn over the young man's body by will, they will take it by force. From that moment, incidents become more intensive and intense and a classical armed conflict began. Until then, or rather by that time, the population was homogenised and resettled to the location of Kozici and Stjenice villages. In parallel with this process, in April 1992 the Muslim population left en masse by buses and passenger vehicles towards Sarajevo. It is estimated that over 3.000 Muslims left Rogatica in this way before the 21st of May, 1992. When the conflict began in Rogatica, the remaining Muslim population, organised by their own leadership, left towards Gorazde and Zepa so that few Muslim families remained in town in comparison to those who had left before. This is a short summary of this witness's statement and with your leave, Your Honours, I would like to ask just a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look up in e-court paragraph 9 of the exhibit which now has the number of D652.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You, Witness, will soon seen it before you and have the opportunity to read it. It's paragraph 9. You say that Muslim representatives accepted this approach. So the decision was made at a regular meeting of the Rogatica Municipal Assembly to divide the municipality into two parts, one Muslim, one Serb. My question is could you briefly describe this process of dividing the municipality, what actually happened on the ground in Rogatica at that time? You will see on another screen the LiveNote and when you see that the typing has stopped, would you only then start to speak so that everything can be properly recorded. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. In the briefest term possible, time had done its work and there were great tensions among the two ethnic communities that formed the majority of the population. The question was how to deal with these tensions. Crisis Staffs were already in place, both the SDA Crisis Staff and the SDS Crisis Staff. Those were the two main political parties that had won the previous elections. I found myself a member of such a team that was extended. I myself and a number of my business associates were not members of the SDS. Talks were held individually and in groups. I was speaking on behalf of the Crisis Staff of the Serbian Democratic Party and I was talking to the Muslim chief of their Crisis Staff. We had some talks at tete-a-tete and also talks between delegations which at that time consisted of three members. We were trying to make an assessment and to and to make a forecast, but the main purpose was to diffuse tensions and resolve the situation peacefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you. This decision made by the municipal assembly to divide the municipality, did it mean a territorial division of Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was one of the realisations made during these talks between two Crisis Staffs. It had already become the practice in Bosnia-Herzegovina to divide municipalities on ethnic principles and we tried to do the same in a working-group made up of representatives of both ethnicities. We were trying to find a way to divide the municipality in such a way that both parts of the municipality would have the majority population of one ethnic group. And we tried basically to respect the ethnic composition as it was in 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell the Court, how did it come about that you became chairman of the Crisis Staff while you were not a member of the SDS? Your political affiliation was quite different, you belonged to the socialists.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I'll try to explain. I was a businessman, a native of Rogatica. I was engaged in what was then referred to as social work. I had already been head of a trade union. I was president of the municipality for two terms, then vice-president of the municipality for two terms. My political affiliation was to the Socialist Alliance which was a multi-national party close to the centre or centre left. And in our environment, I was one of the leading people with an exemplary biography, and obviously there occurred a moment in the work of those Crisis Staffs where everybody felt the kind of saturation and we were under the pressure of these ethnic tensions. So I, who grew up in a multi-ethnic community and had an urban culture, so I was offered that position. But the idea was not to dismiss anyone, just to add to the group, people of a different brand, businessmen with a different kind of thinking who were not members of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please look at paragraph 13. Here, you say that after the entire process which you have described, you know that the equipment of the Territorial Defence was divided between Serbs and Muslims. My question is how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, all this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I don't see where it says that this was after the process we've just been discussing and actually I'm not sure which process that referred to. So I'd just request that the question be clarified slightly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you either clarify or rephrase. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that is perfectly fine, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 13, you dealt with this matter but I must ask you first: This process of dividing the equipment of the Territorial Defence between Serbs and Muslims, did it precede the decision to establish two municipalities in Rogatica or after?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: That's a good question. It happened before, because the atmosphere was such that, for instance, it all began with the division of the police force. We began dividing office space, the police station was divided into two parts. The same happened with the Territorial Defence building. In the basement there were depots of the equipment both of the Territorial Defence and the police. I don't know what kind of weaponry they had and how they got hold of it, but the reference here is to the equipment that was there at the moment. First of all, the police was divided, wherein a session was held, I would say, in a very relaxed atmosphere when members of the police force split into two parts and continued sharing the same building. Sometime later, I can't say how long exactly, the Territorial Defence was divided in the same way and divided the equipment. There must be some record in the archives still somewhere but it was done in a very civilised way, and the two parts of the TO continued to share the same office space, the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now focus on paragraph 14. You say after that the Muslims left Rogatica going towards Zepa and Gorazde. The Muslim political leadership and their authorities were engaged in organising this departure of Muslims. First of all, let me ask you: Territorially and administratively in that period in May 1992, was Zepa part of Rogatica municipality?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Zepa was the largest local commune in Rogatica municipality, 40 kilometres from the centre of town. It was almost completely Muslim in terms of population. Let me just remind you that the population of Rogatica was two-thirds and one-third Serb. Considering this departure of Muslims, at that moment a division was already in place so people from Rogatica went to join their families in Zepa even before that. But this organised departure was by buses, dozens of buses and passenger vehicles, towards Sarajevo. And I know roughly that in this convoy, there were about 2.500 to 3.000 Muslims, which indicates that most of the Muslim population completely freely decided to move towards Sarajevo. Excuse me, the question was here under which leadership. After that, the second half of the Muslim population would leave in a completely organised manner, organised by their leadership in two direction, one towards Medjedja and the other half would go to the west going down to Ustipraca and then up again towards Gorazde. I have to describe to you the route they took. They went through territories populated mainly by Muslims which were later left abandoned. Most of the population had left. And the Serb houses there were mostly destroyed. And on this journey, on both journeys, in both directions, there were killings. Killings against Serbs, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a similar process involved in terms of the Serb population leaving Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in two stages if you can put it that way. In these bad times, March, the beginning of April, many Serbs left and took their children most often to Serbia. People would move out into the outskirts of Rogatica, mostly based on ethnic affiliation, so a lot of Serbs left the centre of Rogatica and for a while Rogatica was practically under the control of the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sokolovic, thank you. And now I am going to let my colleague, the Prosecutor, put his questions to you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was on my mind as well, Mr. Stojanovic, that I would give an opportunity to the Prosecution to cross-examine the witness. Mr. Sokolovic, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. You find him to your right. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can exhibit P3913 be brought to the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, we see here a report on the work of the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Rogatica for the period April to June 1992. Are you familiar with this report?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you assist in preparing it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, because I insisted that this kind of document be drafted and adopted within a certain procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And to whom was it sent?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, all the assemblymen or the municipal assembly had it in their hands. This was already the Serb municipality of Rogatica and I think that it was sent to many addresses at higher levels of government, not only at a local level, if you will.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say "higher levels of government," did that include the Presidency of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think it did, but primarily people who were in charge like the vice-president of the assembly, people who had coordination with the municipality, so several addressees, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It says that the Crisis Staff in the first paragraph was established at a session of the Main Board of the SDS. Was the report also sent to SDS at the republic level?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, this Crisis Staff from 1 to 22, it was organised at the level of the municipality, and as far as I know it was not the subject of any debate or discussion or confirmation or reconfirmation or decision-making by the SDS, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I think you've answered a different question than the one I asked. What I asked was simply was this report sent to the SDS at the republic level?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. But there were members of the Main Board from Rogatica who certainly had access to this material and they may have sent it on further.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And one of those was Rajko Kusis, right, who was a member of the Main Board from Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Kusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see his name at point 5; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Kusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think what you're indicating in your answer is that it's spelled with two Ss with diacritics in the document but in fact, the second S should be a C; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Kusic, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the people we see on the list are all Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the headquarters of the Crisis Staff at this time was in the "sladara" [phoen], malt factory; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the malt factory, that is what it was called, Tvornica Slada.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: How regularly were you yourself present in the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, there were only sessions that were held from time to time, spontaneously, depending on when this was needed. But I attended all sessions of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Over the course of -- you were president of the Crisis Staff for almost three months; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Roughly how many days during that time were you present in the headquarters in your -- to your best recollection?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you see it wasn't the official headquarters. These were offices. Societal offices at the malt factory where we moved after things happened on St. George's day in 1992. We moved out and practically the seat of the administration, we can put it that way, of the municipality of Rogatica moved to the business administration premises of the malt factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that's after roughly the 20th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Basically after St. George's day, especially after the 20th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Then I'd like to look at another document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, your initial question has not been answered. If you're happy with that, I'll leave it to that. But I'll --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're correct, Your Honour, and you've refreshed my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: During that period after St. George's day, up to the time that you stopped being president of the Crisis Staff, roughly how many times were you present in the malt factory?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, practically this was my work place because already in May I was president of the Executive Board and those are the offices where different meetings were held. These are working offices and staff meetings were always held sometime in the afternoon, whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Everybody's present at their workplace a slightly different amount of time, but were you there four days a week, five days a week, seven days a week?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand that question. Do you mean active work in the Crisis Staff or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All I mean for the moment is how often were you in the building that you described as your workplace? Was it once a week, four times a week, seven times a week?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No. You see in principle, every day, unless I was on a business trip or some meeting that was not held right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: With that I will turn to another document unless the Chamber has any additional questions on that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit P3909, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, we see here a report on the work of the Rogatica Municipal Assembly's Executive Committee and it's dated the 1st of October, 1993. Is that your name and signature on the cover page, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No, it's the signature of the secretary of the Executive Board. At the same time, he was secretary of the assembly and of the Executive Board, and in the previous period while the Crisis Staff operated he was the secretary of the Crisis Staff as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And is there a "za" in Serbian before your title to signify that's he's signing for you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, did you also participate in the drafting of this report?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the essence. I know the essence and the secretary worked out the outline, and then I shaped it together with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this one --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Actually, if we could have page 33 in the English and 30 in the B/C/S. And what I'm interested in is below the three Xs for the moment, at the very bottom of the page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So this report, like the previous one, went to committee members. It also went to the command of the Rogatica Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm going to be very precise here because we made this report in 100 copies, we distributed one -- actually 50 to the members of the assembly of Rogatica and the rest different institutions. The Presidency, members of government, members of parliament, of the republic assembly, that is, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As well as the Rogatica Brigade, the Drina Corps command received a copy; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, and also the police structures. Our wish was to have this document reach as many addresses as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we turn to the next page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it also went to the headquarters of the Bosnian Serb army; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think the Ministry of Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If could turn to page 5 in the English and 4 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Below point 2, we read that: "Establishment of Rogatica Municipal Assembly, earlier Serb municipality of Rogatica, as council members know, was carried out at the end of December 1991, and it was composed of all Serb council members, elected at the first multi-party elections in 1990, total 20 members. Serb municipal assembly included also, as per instructions --"

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. We haven't been receiving interpretation for quite a while now since the Prosecutor started asking this question, so I just wanted to draw your attention to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could then -- Mr. Traldi, could you restart and -- and was it from where Mr. Traldi started reading?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the beginning of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From when this question started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please restart, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I take it that I understand correctly that you're receiving interpretation now, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So I'm reading the second paragraph, under point 2 reads: "Establishment of Rogatica Municipal Assembly, earlier Serb Municipality Rogatica, as council members know, was carried out at the end of December 1991, and it was composed of all Serb council members, elected at the first multi-party elections in 1990, total 20 members. Serb Municipal Assembly included also, as per instructions of the Main Serb Democratic Party Board, SDS village board presidents for from the area of the municipality -- total 11." I'll stop there. Sir, what you were reporting was that the municipality -- the municipal assembly was composed entirely of Serb members; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to note an important difference here. This document, you see the one we're reading now, that is from 1991 when this was some kind of inertia, if I can put it that way, and this municipal assembly as far as I know did not hold a single session as such involving that composition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, no one asked you about whether that assembly convened. The question was whether it was composed of Serbs exclusively. Whether it convened or not is a different question. Yes, the witness confirms that that was the case. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, just in response to the last bit of testimony you provided, in paragraph 2 of your statement, you say in pertinent part --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could have it on the screen, please. It's D652.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So at the end of this second paragraph, you say: "At the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992, I served as a deputy in the Rogatica Municipal Assembly." Now you don't make any mention in this paragraph that this assembly never met or wasn't carrying out its functions, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Please let us clarify this. I was president of the assembly of the municipality of Rogatica, and that's what I say here, in the period from 1983 until 1985. As for being a member of the assembly of Rogatica, I was that from 1978 until 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You've read two sentences, neither of which is the one I read to you. So I put to you again, you say here: "At the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992, I served as a deputy in the Rogatica Municipal Assembly." You don't make any suggestion in your statement that that assembly had stopped meeting or wasn't carrying out its functions, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I really want us to understand each other. I did not understand what period you were asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking about the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992. You served as a deputy in the Rogatica Municipal Assembly at that time; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And when you describe that in your statement, you don't make the claim that you just made in your testimony, that that assembly wasn't meeting, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Please, these are different periods. I was a member of the Municipal Assembly of Rogatica, let me not go back to that all the time, but let's just look at the 1990s. Let's look at the first multi-party elections until 1992, for instance. When -- I mean the municipality of Rogatica was divided into two municipalities, and then I remained as a member of the assembly of the Serb municipality of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn back to the previous document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I hope you are aware that you're not answering the question. The question was: When you refer to the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992 when, as you state, you served as a deputy in the Rogatica Municipal Assembly, you do not say a word about that assembly not convening, not meeting. That is what Mr. Traldi was asking you and until now, you have not given an answer. If you're able to answer that question, please do it right away and otherwise, Mr. Traldi will proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, I was in the regular municipal assembly in 1991 and in 1992, that is to say, the one that was elected during the multi-party elections all the way up to the moment where there was this division into two municipalities. I took part in this regular work of the regular assembly and its sessions. This assembly that had been elected at the multi-party elections. Am I being clear on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's have the previous document back, P3909, page 5 in the English and page 4 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this is again the report that you're sending, that you're crafting together with the secretary and sending to the Presidency, the headquarters of the army, and others. Now, it says here -- you and the secretary write: "Establishment of Rogatica municipal assembly, earlier Serb municipality Rogatica, as council members know, was carried out at the end of December 1991 ..." So you're informing the Presidency, the Main Staff, the police, the Drina Corps, the members of the assembly themselves, that this is when this assembly was created; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Please, what is referred to here is what is stated in the archives, that the Serb municipality of Rogatica was established then in accordance with these guidelines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, apparently --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In both the documents, reference is made to the Rogatica Municipal Assembly. Were there two institutions known by that same name at that time, that is, late 1991, early 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, two bodies. Because I would say that this was basically a political decision, and the municipal assembly was elected at the multi-party elections and it continued to function. As far as I know, they held only one such session and I did not take part in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So first, I'd put to you here you are reporting to the president, the Main Staff, and others specifically about the assembly that was established at the end of December 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: You see, first of all we make a report for the municipal assembly of Rogatica, but primarily when the Serb municipality of Rogatica functioned, and that's 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is it your evidence now that the information that you're providing here to the Presidency, the Main Staff, and others is not correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I think they are all correct -- sorry, I just have to say something. There's this introduction here. I talk about the period when I was president of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Rogatica and that was the intention, my intention and the intention of the Executive Board, to represent this, so this is an introduction and the essence is that we want to represent the time when I became president of the Executive Board until the expiry of my term of office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, could we perhaps try to find a formulation that we talk about. Apparently there are two municipal assemblies, Rogatica municipal assemblies. If we call the one the elected Rogatica municipal assembly and the other one, which if I understand you well, was established in December 1991, we call that one, the December Rogatica municipal assembly so that we have clear different wording for the two different municipality assemblies. I suggest that we proceed in that way but not today, but tomorrow. Witness, would you also clearly in your answers distinguish between the one and the other, that is the elected Rogatica municipal assembly and the December Rogatica municipal assembly. We'll adjourn for the day but I would first like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, not to speak or communicate in any other way with whomever it may be, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and we resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 23rd of September, in this same courtroom, I, at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 23rd day of September, 2014 at 9.30 a.m. 24 25
